group: TAS — Trading At Settlement, financial and metals (inventory rows 13, 15, 18, 25, 33, 38; 17 roots)
is_trade_type_variant:
BOTH THINGS ARE TRUE AT ONCE, and the resolution is evidence-based, not a guess.

(a) The daily close of every one of my six shapes IS a settlement instant. CME's own "Daily Settlement Time Details" page states the daily settlement determination ranges: Gold "13:29:00-13:30:00 ET", Silver "13:24:00-13:25:00 ET", Platinum "13:03:00-13:05:00 ET", Copper "12:59:00-13:00:00 ET", Palladium "12:58:00-13:00:00 ET", Treasuries "13:59:30-14:00:00 CT". Converted, those end instants are 12:30 / 12:25 / 12:05 / 12:00 / 12:00 CT and 14:00 CT — an exact, six-for-six match to the closes in the schedule file. So the trap the brief warns about is live here: read naively, these are six settlement fixings, not six session closes.

(b) But CME ALSO publishes these as trading sessions in its own hours tables, distinct from the underlying's, and dates changes to them. On CME's metals trading-hours page (captures 2011-10-29 through 2015-03-22) "Gold TAS", "Silver TAS" and "Copper TAS" are their own product rows, with their own Pre-Open and their own "Electronic Trading (Sunday)" / "Electronic Trading (Weekday)" values — 18:00-13:30 / 18:00-13:25 / 18:00-13:00 ET — sitting two rows away from "Gold Futures & Options ... 18:00-17:15 ET". And CME Globex Notice 2016-12-19 changes a TAS product's hours in exactly session language: "the trading hours for the European Low Sulphur Gasoil (100mt) Bullet Futures Trade at Settlement (TAS) cease daily at 11:30 a.m. Eastern time (ET). Currently, the trading session closes daily at 12:00 p.m. ET."

So: TAS is a trade type whose instruments are nonetheless given their own CME Globex security groups (tag 1151) and their own published session window, whose close happens to be defined by the underlying's settlement instant. That is NOT "the underlying's session", and it is NOT the event-contract failure mode (a per-contract expiry misread as a daily close) — the Close state recurs on every trade date for the security group, and CME's rulebook Rule 524 says the Exchange sets "the products, contract months and time periods during which TAS and TAM transactions shall be permitted" and that a TAS-eligible contract has a "prescribed pre-open time period" of its own.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MODELLING: no root in this group may reuse the underlying's key. Mapping GCT to globex_energy or ZNS to globex_interest_rates would report the market tradeable for 2-4 hours a day after TAS trading has closed — an executable-hours error, the class the repo ranks most serious. Both keys already exclude TAS by their documented scope (futures_profile.rs:148 "Excludes TAS/TAM/BTIC"; verification.md globex_energy "TAS/TAM/BTIC, options, and different product clocks are excluded").

Note also that the queue grid is CME-wide-per-trade-type, not per-product: the pause/pre-open sequence is identical across all TAS groups (see evidence item 3), while only the close differs by product. So the family boundary is per-underlying-metal (and per Treasury complex), not per trade type.

evidence:
All CME paths 403 from this host ("This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity"), including /content/dam/ PDFs, so everything below is CME's own content served through web.archive.org id_ passthrough, except the CME client-site wiki, which served normally.

=== 1. Rulebook: the Exchange sets TAS time periods and a TAS-specific pre-open ===
NYMEX Rulebook Chapter 5, Rule 524 "TRADING AT SETTLEMENT ("TAS") AND TRADING AT MARKER ("TAM") TRANSACTIONS":
  "The Exchange shall determine the products, contract months and time periods during which TAS and TAM transactions shall be permitted."
  524.A.1: "A TAS order may be entered on Globex at any time the applicable contract is available for TAS trading on Globex and during such TAS-eligible contract's prescribed pre-open time period. The initiation of any TAS order on Globex outside these time periods is prohibited."
https://web.archive.org/web/20231206165437id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/content/dam/cmegroup/rulebook/NYMEX/1/5.pdf
(The Rule 524 TAS/TAM Table the chapter points to is https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/files/tas-tam-eligibility.xlsx — retrieved at https://web.archive.org/web/20260830100729id_/... — and contains sheets "Metals TAS" and "Treasury TAS". It publishes eligible contract months ONLY; a full string sweep of the workbook found no hours anywhere in it.)

=== 2. CME publishes the metals TAS windows as sessions, distinct from the underlying (DECISIVE for rows 15/18/25) ===
CME trading-hours page http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/metals-hours.html. Column headers: "Pre-Open Electronic Trading (Sunday) | Electronic Trading (Sunday) | Pre-Open Electronic Trading (Weekday) | Electronic Trading (Weekday) | Open Outcry | CME ClearPort".

=== 3. CME dates changes to a TAS product's trading hours in session language ===
CME Globex Notice, December 19 2016 (repeated 2016-12-26 and 2017-01-02): "European Low Sulphur Gasoil (100mt) Bullet Futures Trade at Settlement Change — Effective Sunday, January 8 (trade date Monday, January 9), the trading hours for the European Low Sulphur Gasoil (100mt) Bullet Futures Trade at Settlement (TAS) cease daily at 11:30 a.m. Eastern time (ET). === 4. The TAS market-state sequence is common to ALL TAS groups, and its pre-open is randomized ===
CME Group client site (public, unauthenticated), "Trade at Settlement - TAS", page 457223974, version 2, 2025-01-13:
  "To ensure appropriate and efficient messaging practices for TAS orders into CME Globex, the timing of each TAS groups' pre-open state is randomized. The market state sequence for TAS groups has a market pause, communicated via the market data Security Status message (tag 35-MsgType=f), tag 326-SecurityTradingStatus=2 at 16:00:00 on Sunday and 16:45:00 Monday through Thursday. TAS groups then go into pre-open on Sundays between 16:00:00 and 16:01:00 Central time (CT), and Mondays through Thursdays between 16:45:00 and 16:46:00 CT."
https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EPICSANDBOX/pages/457223974/Trade+at+Settlement+-+TAS
This matches the 2012-2014 hours pages verbatim ("16:00-16:01 CT" / "16:45-16:46 CT") and matches the 2026 feed, where every one of my six groups pauses at exactly 16:00:00 CT Sunday / 16:45:00 CT Mon-Thu and pre-opens 34-40 seconds later. A future author must model that queue onset as the published one-minute window, never as a fixed instant.

blockers:
Ordered by what actually blocks a key.

1. NO CME-PUBLISHED TAS SESSION WINDOW EXISTS AFTER 2015-03-22, for any product in this group. CME retired /trading_hours/ (the metals page 301s from 2015-09-06 onward) and never replaced it for TAS: a CDX prefix sweep of cmegroup.com/markets/metals/ (1,177 URLs) and cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/ (2,412 URLs) found no TAS product page, so the modern product-page hours module simply has no TAS entry. Until a modern CME statement is found, every current close in this group rests on the weekly TradingSessionList alone, which the repo's law says only seeds. Routes still worth trying, in order: (a) CME Reference Data API v3, https://refdata.api.cmegroup.com/refdata/v3/tradingSchedules, documented at cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net page 457217339 (v8, 2026-08-21) as giving "two years of trading schedules, including 1 year of historical schedules and 1 year forward-looking schedules" keyed by "applicableGlobexGroupCodes" with marketEventType "preopen/open/paused/pcp/closed" — query group codes TG, MT, HT, PE, PX, AT, QT, UT, VT, WT, XT; I could not test it because this host is blocked at cmegroup.com and I did not attempt an unauthenticated call to the api subdomain. (b) The CFTC rule-filing route named in my brief — CME/COMEX/NYMEX/CBOT self-certifications for each TAS listing, which normally recite trading hours where the Globex notice does not. sirt.cftc.gov redirects to https://www.cftc.gov/IndustryOversight/IndustryFilings/TradingOrganizations, which I did not work through. (c) The 25 unfetched 2015-2021 weekly Globex notices.

2. THE THREE UNRESOLVED SHAPES HAVE NO PUBLISHED WINDOW AT ALL — not now, not ever, in anything I retrieved. Platinum TAS (2017-05-22), Palladium TAS (2018-11-19) and Treasury TAS (2021-11-15) all launched after CME stopped publishing TAS hours rows, and their launch notices state products and group codes but no times.
